miyako.title: Guide-Ya-San
miyako.sub: dive shop · call this one first
miyako.note: With the Advanced course ruled out, this is the shop built around what you actually want: diving Open Water divers well. Caps at four guests per guide, so six of you means two guides, and runs a named tour for certified divers and beginners together.
miyako.book: English booking form on their site, or phone between 08:00 and 22:00. Say all six are Open Water, two days on 22–23 October, no course. Ask them to name the sites — you want Nakanoshima Channel, Twin Caves, Mini Toriike and the Wonderful Cave grottoes.
miyako.when: Now. Late October is high season and you need two consecutive days.
miyako.meta: Ratio: 4 guests per guide · Mixed levels: named tour · Record: 18 yrs clean · Your plan: 2 days, no course

miyako.title: Aquatic Adventure
miyako.note: Takes Open Water divers happily and runs the newest boat of the four. It also teaches the Advanced course, which you have decided against — so the reason it used to rank first no longer applies.
miyako.book: Email with the full picture: six divers, all Open Water, two days 22–23 October, no course. Reviews call the instructor’s English functional rather than fluent, so put the site list in writing.
miyako.when: Enquire in parallel with Guide-Ya-San — whoever answers well gets the booking.
miyako.meta: Takes: intro → advanced · Boat: Estrella de Agua, 2023 · Your plan: 2 days, no course

miyako.title: Penguin Divers
miyako.note: Owner’s husband Joe is Fijian and a native English speaker — the only shop where English is a first language rather than a service.
miyako.book: Email is the reliable route. Phone unverified: directory listings disagree on the number.
miyako.when: Worth an email if English clarity turns out to be the sticking point elsewhere.
miyako.meta: English: native speaker · Size: small groups

miyako.title: Sea turtle snorkelling
miyako.note: Miyako’s green turtles sit in shallow, sheltered water and the operators here quote encounter rates at or near 100% — which, unusually for that kind of claim, is borne out by the reviews. No experience required, wetsuits provided, and most plans include hotel pickup and photos.
miyako.book: Now that nobody is diving on the 24th, book this for all six as the morning of that day. Several operators bundle it with clear SUP for not much more, which would cover the whole day in one booking.
miyako.when: Book a week or two out. Compare on the aggregator rather than going direct — the same boats are listed across all of them.
miyako.meta: Length: half day · Cost: ≈ ¥6,000–8,000 · Suits: complete beginners · Pickup: usually included

miyako.title: Yukishio Salt Museum
miyako.note: Holds a Guinness record for the most minerals in a salt. That sounds like nothing until you taste it next to ordinary salt. Short free tour, and the salt soft-serve is much better than it has any right to be.
miyako.book: No booking. Drop in on the 25th on the way to or from Ikema — it is right on that road.
miyako.when: Buy the salt here; it is the best small souvenir on the island.
miyako.meta: Cost: free · Length: ~20 min · Where: northern tip, near Ikema

miyako.title: Awamori distillery
miyako.note: Okinawa’s rice spirit, distilled on the island. The aged kusu is nothing like the harsh young awamori that puts people off it — closer to a soft rum. Both Taragawa and Ikema pour.
miyako.book: Ring ahead if you want the tour rather than just the shop counter; the tasting itself is walk-in.
miyako.when: Nominate a driver. Two cars makes this easy — the drinkers go in one.
miyako.meta: Cost: free–¥1,000 · Length: ~45 min · Where: both near Hirara

miyako.title: Pumpkin Rock kayak & SUP
miyako.note: Paddle to a limestone sea cave holding a huge pumpkin-shaped formation. Usually bundled with reef snorkelling. The Shimajiri mangrove paddle is the calmer alternative.
miyako.book: Ask your dive shop first — most Miyako operators run these or will point you at whoever does. Otherwise book through Activity Japan.
miyako.when: Slot it on the 25th, your no-fly day.
miyako.meta: Length: half day · Effort: low · Suits: everyone

kakunodate.title: Lake Tazawa cruise
kakunodate.sub: and your inn is on the shore
kakunodate.note: Japan’s deepest lake at 423 m — which is why it never freezes and why the blue is that improbable. Your dates catch the very end of the season, so this is a now-or-not-this-trip item. Katakurinohana sits on the lake, so it is a short drive rather than an outing.
kakunodate.book: Confirm it is still sailing when you ring the inn about the late check-in — the closing date moves with the weather each year, and 2026 timings are published as a PDF.
kakunodate.when: Best slotted into the 28th after Nyuto, or the morning of the 29th before you drive north.
kakunodate.meta: Season: late Apr – early Nov · Length: ~40 min · Cost: ≈ ¥1,200 · From: Shirahama pier

kakunodate.title: Tsurunoyu Onsen · day bathing
kakunodate.note: Thatched buildings, milky-white sulphur water, and a large mixed open-air bath. The most famous bath in Tohoku.
kakunodate.book: Phone reservation advised — day-use capacity is limited and it is taken by phone, in Japanese. Closed Monday mornings for cleaning; your Wednesday is fine. If full, Taenoyu faces a waterfall and Kuroyu and Ganiba are both excellent.
kakunodate.when: Ring a few weeks out. Ask the inn at Katakurinohana to call for you if the language is a barrier.

kakunodate.title: Dakigaeri Gorge
kakunodate.sub: 27 Oct · peak foliage on your dates
kakunodate.note: Ten kilometres of gorge along a mineral blue-green river, maples right over the water, a red suspension bridge and the Kaiun-no-taki waterfall. The single best walk of the trip and it costs nothing.
kakunodate.book: No entry fee and nothing to reserve. Parking fills with coach traffic from mid-morning — the only booking that matters is your own start time.
kakunodate.when: Be there by 09:15. A Tuesday morning in season is as quiet as it gets.
kakunodate.meta: Entry: free · Drive: 15 min from town · Walk: 1.5–4 h · Festival: runs in season

kakunodate.title: Aoyagi-ke samurai house
kakunodate.note: The grandest of the Kakunodate samurai residences — a compound of several small museums, an armoury and gardens behind a black wooden gate.
kakunodate.book: Walk-in, pay at the gate. Allow an hour; it is bigger inside than it looks from the street.

kakunodate.title: Ishiguro-ke samurai house
kakunodate.sub: 27 Oct · the oldest, still lived in
kakunodate.note: The oldest surviving samurai house in Kakunodate, and the only one where the family still lives upstairs. Smaller than Aoyagi-ke and considerably more atmospheric for it.
kakunodate.book: Walk-in. Opening hours are shorter than Aoyagi-ke and can vary — check on the day.
kakunodate.when: Nothing to reserve, but go before 16:00.
kakunodate.meta: Entry: small charge · Age: oldest in the district · Note: family still resides

kakunodate.title: Kabazaiku Denshokan
kakunodate.note: Wild cherry bark shaved, polished and laminated onto tea caddies and boxes until it glows reddish-brown. Invented here by low-ranking samurai as a side income. Craftsmen work on site.
kakunodate.book: Walk-in. The shop sells the real thing — tea caddies are the buy, and they last decades.
kakunodate.meta: Craft: exists only here · Age: ~2 centuries · Watch: artisans at work

kakunodate.title: Ando Jozo · miso & soy brewery
kakunodate.note: A working miso and soy-sauce brewery in a Meiji-era brick storehouse on the main street. You can walk into the warehouse itself, which is the point.
kakunodate.book: Free entry to the shop and warehouse. Buy the miso — it travels.
kakunodate.when: Nothing to reserve. Open through the afternoon.
kakunodate.meta: Founded: 19th century · Free: to walk in

kakunodate.title: Suzuki Shuzo · Hideyoshi sake
kakunodate.note: One of Akita’s long-standing breweries, making Hideyoshi in Kakunodate itself, a few doors from Ando Jozo. Akita’s cold winters and soft water are why this prefecture brews as well as it does.
kakunodate.book: Shop is walk-in for tasting and buying. Brewery tours, if running, need arranging ahead — ask the tourist office by the station.
kakunodate.when: Ask about tours a few days out if anyone wants one.

kakunodate.title: Taenoyu
kakunodate.note: Arguably the more beautiful bath of the two — an open-air pool looking straight at a waterfall, with two different spring sources. The one to take if Tsurunoyu is full.
kakunodate.book: Day bathing in a narrow window, 10:30–14:00. Ring ahead; capacity is small.
kakunodate.when: Have this number with you on the 28th as the live fallback.
kakunodate.meta: Day use: 10:30–14:00 · Price: ¥800 · Bath: faces a waterfall

kakunodate.title: Kuroyu Onsen
kakunodate.note: Thatched buildings and milky sulphur water, with the widest day-use window in the valley — the practical choice if you arrive later than planned.
kakunodate.book: Day bathing 09:00–16:00, ¥600. No reservation needed for day use.
kakunodate.when: No booking. The safety net if the morning overruns.
kakunodate.meta: Day use: 09:00–16:00 · Price: ¥600 · Water: sulphurous, cloudy

kakunodate.title: Ganiba Onsen
kakunodate.note: The quietest of the group, with an open-air bath set among beech trees a short walk from the building. Least visited, and in late October that is the whole appeal.
kakunodate.meta: Day use: 09:00–15:30 · Price: ¥600 · Feature: beech-forest rotenburo

aomori.title: Apple picking · Hirosaki Apple Park
aomori.sub: and you are here at peak Fuji
aomori.note: Aomori grows more than half of Japan’s apples, and picking runs to mid-November — which puts you squarely in Fuji season, the best of them and the last to ripen. Around eighty varieties in the park.
aomori.book: No booking needed. Slots straight into the 31st alongside Hirosaki Castle and the cider, which is the strongest version of that day.
aomori.when: Confirm the picking is still running that week — it depends on the harvest, not the calendar.
aomori.meta: Season: 1 Aug – mid-Nov · Cost: a few hundred yen · Varieties: ~80 · Where: Hirosaki, ~1 hr

aomori.title: Tsugaru-jamisen, live
aomori.sub: Hirosaki · the best evening on this leg
aomori.note: Forget the polite image of shamisen — Tsugaru style is percussive, furiously fast, and played a metre from your table while you eat Tsugaru food. Most visitors never think to do this, and it is the thing people remember about Aomori years later.
aomori.book: Three venues in Hirosaki do it properly: Anzu, Aiya and Adohadari. Rooms are small — book a table for six rather than turning up.
aomori.when: Pairs with the 31st if you take the Hirosaki option, since you are already there.
aomori.meta: Where: Anzu, Aiya, Adohadari · Cost: dinner + cover · Sets: through the evening · Book: yes, small rooms

aomori.title: A-Factory cidre works
aomori.note: A glass-walled cider works in the harbour building — you watch it being made, then drink it. Kimori and the house flight run dry through to sweet, all from Aomori apples. Also the best place in the city to buy apple everything.
aomori.book: No booking. The obvious use of a spare hour before dinner on any of the four Aomori evenings.
aomori.when: Walkable from Art Hotel Aomori, so it survives bad weather and tired legs.
aomori.meta: Cost: tasting flight · Length: ~1 hr · Where: harbour, by the station · Open: late

aomori.title: Tsugaru-han Neputa Village
aomori.note: Neputa floats, live shamisen through the day, craft demonstrations, and goldfish-neputa painting you can take home. Not high art, but a genuinely good two hours if the 31st turns wet and the mountain roads shut.
aomori.book: Walk in. Worth holding in reserve rather than planning — it is the fallback that makes a bad-weather 31st fine instead of wasted.
aomori.when: Next to the castle park, so it combines with the apples and the cider.
aomori.meta: Length: ~2 hrs · Where: beside Hirosaki Castle · Indoors: entirely

aomori.title: Hakkoda Ropeway
aomori.note: A 100-person cabin to Tamoyachi-dake. By 30 Oct the summit itself will likely be bare or frosted — the range views and the road up are the real payoff.
aomori.book: No advance booking — buy at the station. But it stops for high wind as often as for snow, so ring on the morning before you commit to the hour’s drive.
aomori.when: Call the morning of, from the hotel.
aomori.meta: First car: 09:00 · Every: 15–20 min · Last down: 16:40 · Top: 1,324 m

aomori.title: Sukayu Onsen · thousand-person bath
aomori.note: A vast all-hinoki mixed bathing hall of roughly 260 m². Acidic, milky, and the classic Hakkoda soak — fifteen minutes from the ropeway.
aomori.book: Day bathing is walk-in, no reservation needed. Ring only if you want lunch or a room. Note the women-only hour if that matters to anyone.
aomori.when: No booking. Just turn up between the ropeway and the drive home.

aomori.title: Aoni Onsen · the lamp inn
aomori.note: No electricity by design — lit entirely by oil lamps. Four baths, including a riverside open-air reached across a suspension bridge. Genuinely unlike anywhere else you will go.
aomori.book: Day bathing is available in the daytime, but the road in is narrow and remote — phone ahead to confirm they are open to day visitors that day. Staying the night is also possible and is the fuller experience.
aomori.when: Ring a week out. Pairs with the Hirosaki day.
aomori.meta: Light: oil lamps only · Baths: 4, free-flowing · Access: narrow mountain road

aomori.title: Nebuta Warasse
aomori.note: Five of the previous year’s prize-winning Nebuta floats, lit and at close range — twenty-odd feet of painted washi warriors on wire frames.
aomori.book: Walk-in, tickets at the door. No reservation.
aomori.when: Any evening. Best paired with A-Factory next door for Aomori cider.
aomori.meta: Walk: 5 min from hotel · Indoors: year-round

aomori.title: Sannai-Maruyama
aomori.note: A Jomon settlement occupied for more than a thousand years, with reconstructed pit dwellings and the great six-pillar timber tower. The best bad-weather day in the prefecture.
aomori.book: Walk-in. Free guided tours run through the day — ask at the desk when you arrive, they are worth catching.
aomori.when: No booking. Combine with the art museum next door.
aomori.meta: Drive: 20 min · Mostly: under cover · Next to: the art museum

aomori.title: Aomori Museum of Art
aomori.sub: 1 Nov · next to the Jomon site
aomori.note: Yoshitomo Nara’s four-storey Aomori-ken dog, Shiko Munakata’s woodblocks, and Chagall’s vast painted backdrops for Aleko. One of the best regional museums in Japan.
aomori.book: Walk-in. Check the weekly closing day and whether an exhibition changeover is on before you drive out.
aomori.when: No booking, but confirm opening on the day.
aomori.meta: Drive: 20 min · Holds: Nara, Munakata, Chagall

aomori.title: Osorezan Bodaiji
aomori.sub: 31 Oct · last day of the season
aomori.note: One of the three holiest sites in Japan — a sulphur-blasted crater of grey ash and steaming vents beside a startlingly blue caldera lake, understood as the entrance to the underworld.
aomori.book: Walk-in entry. It shuts on 31 October until May, so ring first to confirm the final day’s hours before committing five hours of driving.
aomori.when: Decide by the 30th. There is no second chance on this trip.
aomori.meta: Season: 1 May – 31 Oct · Drive: 2 h 30 each way · On site: free onsen huts

aomori.title: Lake Towada cruise
aomori.note: A boat across the caldera lake. Its real use is logistical: sail one way and walk Oirase the other, so nobody backtracks.
aomori.book: Tickets at the pier. Check the 2026 timetable before you plan the day around it — season dates and the last sailing move each year.
aomori.when: Confirm the timetable the week before.
aomori.meta: Route: Yasumiya ↔ Nenokuchi · Pairs with: walking Oirase one way

aomori.title: Tsugaru Iwaki Skyline
aomori.note: A toll road up the flank of Mt Iwaki to the 8th station, then a chairlift to just below the 1,625 m summit. The biggest view-to-effort ratio in the region.
aomori.book: Toll paid at the gate, no advance booking. But it closes for the season in early November and shuts in bad weather — ring to confirm the road and the chairlift are both running.
aomori.when: Ring the morning of, before driving to Hirosaki.
aomori.meta: Bends: 69 numbered hairpins · Then: chairlift to near summit · Closes: early November

aomori.title: Hirosaki Park · autumn festival
aomori.note: The Chrysanthemum and Autumn Foliage Festival runs across your dates, with the maples lit after dark. Check whether the castle keep is back on its stone base after the wall repairs before you build the day around it.
aomori.book: Park entry is walk-in; the festival area has a small charge. The tourist association publishes the apple-pie map — pick it up at the station or download it.
aomori.when: Nothing to reserve, but confirm the festival dates and the keep’s status the week before.
aomori.meta: Festival: mid-Oct → early Nov · Drive: 45 min · Also: ~50 mapped apple pies

aomori.title: Furukawa market · nokkedon
aomori.note: Buy a bowl of rice and a book of tickets, then walk the stalls trading tickets for scallop, uni, tuna and roe. You build the bowl yourself.
aomori.book: No booking. Just turn up early with cash.
aomori.when: Check the weekly closing day before you plan the 1st around it.
aomori.meta: Walk: 5 min from hotel · Mornings: only

tokyo.title: Kabuki-za · single act
tokyo.sub: 一幕見席 · bought on the day
tokyo.note: You do not have to commit to four hours of kabuki. Hitomaku-mi single-act tickets are sold on the day at the theatre’s side entrance and get you one act. It is the cheapest genuinely extraordinary hour in Tokyo, and if it turns out not to be for you, you have lost the price of a coffee.
tokyo.book: Ten minutes from Akasaka. Check the day’s programme in the morning and go for whichever act reads best.
tokyo.when: Good for the 19th, or the evening of the 20th once everyone is back from Fuji and Kyoto.
tokyo.meta: Cost: ≈ ¥1,000–2,000 · Length: 30–90 min · Book: no — same day · Where: Ginza

tokyo.title: Sumo morning practice
tokyo.note: Worth knowing before anyone gets their hopes up: Tokyo’s grand tournaments are January, May and September — there is none while you are here. What you can do instead is watch a stable’s morning practice, which is closer, quieter and arguably the better experience.
tokyo.book: Goes through a guide or the hotel concierge; stables do not take direct bookings from visitors. Strict etiquette — silence, no crossed legs, no leaving early.
tokyo.when: Only realistic on the 19th, and only for whoever will genuinely get up for it.
tokyo.meta: Cost: ≈ ¥10,000–15,000 · Start: very early · Book: through a guide

tokyo.title: Street go-karting
tokyo.note: The one Tokyo activity that requires an IDP — which every driver here is carrying anyway for the two car hires. Costumes, public roads, Shibuya and the Rainbow Bridge. Ridiculous, and unlike anything else on this trip.
tokyo.book: Book ahead and upload licence details in advance; operators will not let you drive without the physical IDP on the day.
tokyo.when: Four of you will love this and two probably will not — a good candidate for splitting the evening.
tokyo.meta: Cost: ≈ ¥10,000 · Length: ~2 hrs · Needs: International Driving Permit

tokyo.title: Japan Series, if it lands
tokyo.note: Late October is exactly when the Japan Series runs, and Tokyo Dome is twenty minutes from Akasaka. A Japanese baseball crowd is one of the great sporting experiences anywhere — relentless, organised, brass-band loud, and nothing like a Western stadium.
tokyo.book: Tickets are hard if it does land on the 18th or 19th, but worth ten minutes of trying. Resale sites are the realistic route.
tokyo.when: Check the fixture list once the Climax Series finishes in mid-October.
tokyo.meta: When: late October · Where: Tokyo Dome · Odds: fixture-dependent

tokyo.title: teamLab Planets TOKYO
tokyo.note: The one to do if you only do one. You go barefoot and wade through warm knee-deep water under projected koi, then stand inside a mirrored room of hanging orchids. It is a physical experience, not a screen you look at.
tokyo.book: Timed-entry tickets, online only, through the official store. Wear or bring shorts — you roll trousers up and the water is knee-deep. Bags go in lockers and phones survive fine.
tokyo.when: Book as soon as the 20 October split is settled. Slots genuinely sell out, and tickets for a given month go on sale roughly a month ahead.
tokyo.meta: Length: 75–90 min · You get: wet to the knee · Price: from ≈ ¥3,800 · Open until: end of 2027

tokyo.title: teamLab Borderless TOKYO
tokyo.note: The other Tokyo venue, and a different proposition: works wander between rooms and spill into each other, with no fixed path. Bigger, longer, and better if you have already done Planets — but less of a single physical hit.
tokyo.book: Timed-entry tickets online. Entrance is at Azabudai Hills — take the D elevator down to B1, which is not obvious from the street.
tokyo.when: Same as Planets. If you can only fit one and it is a first visit, take Planets.
tokyo.meta: Length: 2–3 hours · Format: no map, no route · Price: from ≈ ¥3,800 · Shoes: stay on

tokyo.title: Shibuya Sky
tokyo.sub: needs a slot — the 19th is full
tokyo.note: The rooftop deck over Shibuya Crossing. The 19th now runs shrine-to-Senso-ji with no gap, so this needs its own slot — the honest options are a sunset slot instead of Asakusa on the 19th, or working it into the 20th. The free Metropolitan Government deck in Shinjuku is the no-booking fallback.
tokyo.book: Timed-entry tickets online. Sunset slots go first and cost more.
tokyo.when: A week or two ahead is usually enough, except for sunset slots.
tokyo.meta: Height: 229 m · View: 360° · Best at: sunset

tokyo.title: Group dinner · Akasaka, 20 Oct
tokyo.note: The Kyoto party gets back around 22:15 and the Fuji party around 20:00. A late booking lets whoever is back eat together.
tokyo.book: Ask the hotel front desk to book — Via Inn Prime Akasaka sits in the middle of the izakaya quarter and they will know what takes six at short notice.

tokyo.title: Kawaguchiko Tenjozan ropeway
tokyo.note: Up to a deck looking straight across the lake at the mountain, with short trails at the top if legs allow.
tokyo.book: Tickets on site, no advance booking needed.
tokyo.meta: Ride: 3 minutes · From: beside the station
